cards.back: With credentials: sees installed versions and patches, far fewer false positives.
Without credentials: attacker's view, only exposed services and banners.
Internet Protocol Address Management: inventory of IP ranges and addresses, knowing which asset owns an IP.
Cloud Security Posture Management: continuously detects cloud misconfigurations (public buckets, overly broad IAM).
Code review (SAST/DAST) to find hardcoded secrets, injections, and vulnerable dependencies before production.
Severity evaluation: CVSS, exposure, asset criticality, and known exploit combined.
It proves a vulnerability is actually exploitable in context, which a scanner only assumes.
A critical CVSS on an isolated asset may rank below an exposed high on a critical asset: prioritize in context.
CVSS = severity score; CVE = enumeration reference for a public vulnerability.
Patch, update, hardening, disabling service, segmentation, or replacing an EOL product.
Alternative measure when patching is impossible: WAF, segmentation, enhanced monitoring.
Documented decision by the asset owner, with compensating control and review date — never simply forgetting.
Rescan with the same method after remediation, before closing the ticket.

cards.front: Why rescan with the same method?
cards.back: If the method changes, the disappearance of the finding may come from the scanner, not the fix.
Dashboards, remediation timelines, trends: drives prioritization and SLAs.
Customers, partners, regulators: contractual or legal obligations, approved disclosure.
Public reward program for discovering flaws, with defined scope and rules.
Reporting channel, safe harbor for the researcher, and remediation window before publication.
